analyst.summary: Oil India is a profitable, cheaply-valued state-run oil & gas producer (about 10.5x trailing earnings, 17%+ return on equity, manageable debt) whose FY26 consolidated profit grew 7% -- but that growth was carried almost entirely by its refining subsidiary Numaligarh Refinery's unusually strong margins, while Oil India's own core crude-oil business actually saw profit fall roughly 29% for the year on a weaker realised oil price and India's windfall-tax mechanism, which caps how much of any oil-price rally producers get to keep. Reserves are being replenished faster than they are being produced (a genuine long-term positive), and the balance sheet is healthy, so we are not calling this a Sell purely on recent soft share-price momentum. But the recent earnings strength leans heavily on a cyclical refining-margin tailwind rather than the core exploration-and-production business, so we rate it a Hold rather than a name to add to.
